perspectives.snippet: Top comment · Thanks for the info. It reinforces my position that if you really living on a reduced income then you should not have to pay taxes on your SS. The wife and I are in the 85% taxed SS group because I am still working part time and when that runs out I will start drawing on our 401k. When enacted the numbers were reasonable. It would be nice if they would adjust the numbers for inflation. If they did then I suspect that the thresholds would be about twice as much as they are. Had they done that the concept is tax the people who can afford it not those that can not would have continued to be a reasonable description of the program. Without the adjustment there are folks in the middle where the taxes can be somewhat painful to pay.
